varieties.name: Venus
varieties.notes: Quoted verbatim: 'ideal for early to main season production ... popular with customers who prefer aromatic musk melons in the Western Cape, Northern Cape and Free State production areas of South Africa.' Zone keys are an approximation (Northern Cape -> karoo-arid, Free State -> highveld) since the catalog's zone list has no direct Northern Cape/Free State entries.

varieties.name: Colorspring
varieties.notes: Quoted verbatim: 'Ideal for the spring and summer seasons ... Main season 70 - 75 days.' No specific province/zone stated by the supplier.

varieties.name: Orangelly
varieties.notes: Described in a Starke Ayres melon news article as suited to 'early- and late-summer production in various climates'; no specific province stated.

zoneNotes: Starke Ayres' 'Venus' cultivar description is the only source found this session that ties a spanspek/melon variety to specific South African provinces (Western Cape, Northern Cape, Free State), which at least confirms the Western Cape is a real commercial production area for this crop even though a Western Cape-specific sowing-month source could not be found.
gaps: Winter/Western Cape sowMonths (specific months) not sourced: only that the Venus variety is commercially popular in the Western Cape, without a stated sowing window. No Western Cape/Elsenburg-specific melon sowing calendar was retrieved this session.
Transplant status (false) is inferred indirectly from blank seedtray/seedbed columns in KZN DARD's spacing table, rather than an explicit statement that melon is direct-sown.

Additional named varieties (Morgan, Gatsby, Cyclone, Sweet Spring) were seen in a Starke Ayres news article with only general seasonal descriptors ('early-summer', 'mid-summer') and no province-level detail, so they were left out of the varieties list beyond Orangelly.
summary: Frost tenderness, days-to-harvest, row/in-row spacing, seed rate and yield are sourced (KZN DARD Tables 4/5/8), and the Western Cape is confirmed as a real production zone via Starke Ayres' Venus cultivar description. Verdict held to 'partial' because winter/Western Cape sowMonths (specific months) and transplant status remain only indirectly sourced or unsourced.
